text:
ellie: customer reports intermittent truncated JSON from our /v1/stream endpoint when using SSE. they get a partial object and the client fails to parse (schema validation). pasted their snippet below.

ellie: customer says it happens ~1-2% of requests, more often behind their corporate proxy. stack: hosted API, model: rdx-13b, mode: streaming structured JSON.

sara: can you add the request id and timestamp? also whether this is hosted or dedicated for that tenant.

ellie: req_id: c3f9b7a2, time: 2026-02-18T15:02:11Z, host: hosted. here's the exact SSE body they captured (truncated):

ellie: ```
data: {"event":"response","payload":{"id":"abc123","chunks":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello, here is some JSON: {\"items\":[{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"foo\"},{\"id\":2,\"text\":\"bar\"}]\n"}}}

# stream cuts off here - missing closing brackets and final metadata
```

mike: do we see a FIN/RST from the edge for that req_id? could be proxy/keepalive. any NGINX / Cloudflare in the path?

deploy-bot: edge-log: "conn reset by peer" for req_id=c3f9b7a2, upstream 10.42.11.5:443, bytes_sent=1243

alex: i suspect an intermediate layer (proxy or corporate client) truncating idle chunked streams. common culprits: low keepalive timeout on LB or HTTP/2 flow-control. ask customer to try bypassing corp proxy or set curl -N to keep connection open.

vinay: on runtime side we flush KV cache frames and stream tokens as small SSE frames. if an upstream closes mid-chunk you'll see exactly that (partial JSON). runtime currently sends final brace in a separate chunk sometimes. we can attempt to coalesce last N bytes to avoid atomicity issues.

sara: @mike @alex can we get logs (edge + runtime) for req_id c3f9b7a2? and a pcap if customer can provide. also need the client's User-Agent and any proxy headers.

ellie: customer attached a curl reproduction they ran against our hosted endpoint:

ellie: ```bash
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \\n  -H "X-Client-Trace: reproduce-1" \\n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rdx-13b&mode=json"
```

ellie: and the client observed the same cut. they also tried with --http1.1 and got similar behaviour.

alex: ask them to run: `curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -v --raw` and save the raw bytes. that helps us see boundary bytes and whether there are stray CRLFs or truncated UTF-8 sequences.

vinay: for a quick workaround we can recommend the customer enable an SSE keepalive/heartbeat on their client or server side. runtime can emit a comment line `: heartbeat\n` every 15s to keep proxies from timing out. this won't fix a hard RST but reduces timeout-induced closes.

mike: also check if our edge had a 502/504 or health probe during that window. if the edge proactively closed the connection due to backend slowness that could be a root cause.

ellie: customer says they saw a TCP RST from 172.68.53.10 (Cloudflare) in the packet capture. they suspect corporate infra between them and CF as well.

sara: i'm going to open an internal incident ticket and tag eng-runtime. please add any logs you collect. link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-142 (private)

alex: for repro, here's a tiny python server that deliberately splits a JSON object across SSE frame boundaries to mimic the issue. ask customer to run locally and try their client against it: 

alex: ```python
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
import time

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream')
        self.send_header('Cache-Control', 'no-cache')
        self.end_headers()
        frames = ['{"items":[', '{"id":1,"text":"a"},', '{"id":2,"text":"b"}]', '}']
        for f in frames:
            self.wfile.write(b"data: " + f.encode('utf-8') + b"\n\n")
            self.wfile.flush()
            time.sleep(0.5)

HTTPServer(('0.0.0.0', 9000), H).serve_forever()
```

vinay: that reproducer is useful. runtime team: we should consider coalescing the last chunk (e.g., keep last 256 bytes in buffer and send as one write) as a mitigation for proxy truncation. filing a follow-up RFC.

mike: short-term action items: (1) ask customer to bypass corporate proxy and test; (2) ask for raw tcpdump/curl --raw; (3) add temporary SSE heartbeats; (4) eng-runtime to investigate coalescing last bytes.

ellie: customer agreed to try bypassing proxy and will send pcap and raw output later today.

sara: thanks. @mike please pick up the eng-runtime task and update INC-2026-142 with findings. set severity as P2 for customer-impacting parse failures.

mike: on it. i'll post updates here and in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:

ellie: closing loop with customer now, will attach their pcap when received.

# end of thread
